conventions.convention: A scheme morphism is flat when the local-ring map O_{S,s} → O_{X,x} is flat at every source point; flatness at a point is a local-ring-map condition and empty source is flat vacuously.

Smoothness at x means locally finite presentation at x, flatness at x, and geometric regularity of the scheme-theoretic fibre at x after every field extension of κ(s); relative dimension is defined separately and may vary with x.
Relative dimension uses local dimension of geometric-fibre points over x, not the height of O_{Y,y}; pure relative dimension requires the same integer at every source point.
Étale means smooth of relative dimension zero; flat plus unramified is an equivalent criterion only under the locally finite presentation hypothesis stated in the theorem.
For a fixed degree-one-generated Proj presentation, F(d) means F ⊗ O_X(d); a change of embedding or line bundle must be written explicitly and does not silently change the twist.
The finite affine Čech cover is ordered as given; the Čech complex and comparison use that order.

The configuration basepoint is the same explicit ordered tuple Q in the open unit disk, used as [Q] in the closed-disk unordered configuration group; changing basepoint requires a specified connecting path.
Stacking γ above β runs β first, while the fundamental-group product is first loop followed by second; raw slicing reverses products and the group isomorphism uses the inverse loop class.

load_bearing.statement: If X is a quasi-compact separated scheme, U_0,...,U_r a finite affine open cover in the given order, and F is quasi-coherent, every finite intersection is affine and the canonical ordered Čech-to-sheaf cohomology map is an isomorphism for every q ≥ 0. Empty scheme is included; r=0 is the one-member cover.

For a commutative ring A with 1, n ≥ 0, d ∈ Z, and X = P^n_A, H^q(X,O_X(d)) vanishes unless q=0 or q=n. If n>0, H^0 is A[x_0,...,x_n]_d for d ≥ 0 and zero for d<0; H^n is free on Laurent monomials with every exponent negative and total degree d, and is nonzero precisely for d ≤ −n−1 and A ≠ 0. If n=0, H^0 ≅ A for every d and higher groups vanish; A=0 gives zero groups.

Let f:X→S be proper and of finite presentation, S arbitrary, and F coherent and flat over S. For fixed s and q, if the base-change map φ^q_s is surjective, then on an affine neighbourhood U every base change T→U has an isomorphism in degree q; φ^q_s itself is an isomorphism. Under that surjectivity, R^q f_*F is locally free near s iff φ^(q−1)_s is surjective; for q=0 the previous-degree condition is automatic and f_*F is finite locally free near s. AC and DC are assumed.

For a Noetherian commutative ring A, X projective over Spec A via a closed immersion into some P^N_A, an ample invertible sheaf L, and coherent F, there is m_0 such that H^q(X,F⊗L^m)=0 for every q>0 and m≥m_0, with one bound for all q. Empty and zero cases are included; no effective bound is claimed.

A morphism f:X→S is smooth iff it is locally of finite presentation and formally smooth in the local lifting convention: lifts across square-zero thickenings need exist only Zariski-locally on the test scheme, with no uniqueness required. AC is assumed.

For a morphism f locally of finite presentation and x∈X, f is étale at x iff it is flat at x and unramified at x; unramified here means locally finite type and formally unramified, equivalently Ω_{X/S,x}=0. AC is assumed.

At the fixed tuple Q, raw slicing is a bijection from geometric braid-isotopy classes to loops in the interior unordered configuration space and reverses products. Composing the induced map with inclusion into the closed-disk configuration group and inversion gives a group isomorphism. Changing basepoint requires a connecting path; no Artin-presentation completeness claim is made.

concerns.concern: In clause 3, the proof says the base-change argument applies over an open neighbourhood of x, but F3 only states base-change stability for a globally smooth morphism and that smoothness is preserved by restricting the source. It does not explicitly choose an open U containing x on which f|U is smooth and identify U_s as an open in X_s. The conclusion follows from the local definition plus base-change stability, but that localization step should be stated.
